Rows first pinned here, because this family is the only adjudication of a committed §5.1 envelope its own slot refuses and a step that does not fit an L1 transaction leaves the two stalls §12.7's residue paragraph named still open, with nothing else to notice.
spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §12.8 (the fault kind, its adjudication and its boundary against both §12.7's bytes-only verdict and §12.3's fault_item_predicate), with §5.1 for the envelope grammar this family guards on, §5.3/§7.4 for the fixed-stride table and the count-consistency arithmetic, §5.4 for the per-field byte bound, §4/§7.1 for the authenticate-once hash check, §8.3/§8.4 for `K` and the tier-3 partition, and §8.8 for the carriage wire types
note:
§12.8 publishes a cost for the family's step 01 and these rows are that measurement, taken through `run-focused-check.mjs` against `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/committed-field-shape/rule.test.ak`. They split the claim the way the work splits, into a byte term and an item term, and each has a fixture-only control beside it.

**What the claim says.** Authenticate then decide: `authenticated_committed_preimage` materialises whichever §8 tier the prover named and hashes it once against §4's positionally-extracted commitment, `envelope_verdict_v1` then walks §5.1 to the envelope guard, and this section's own two questions — §5.4's byte bound and §7.4's `header_len + stride·N == total_length` — are `O(1)` over a header `minimal_array_header_v1` reads in three bytes. **The dominant term is therefore §12.7's walk, reused rather than restated**, which is why this lane's rows sit within a few percent of §12.7's at the same shapes and why the two ledgers are separate anyway: the fixtures differ (this family's are grammatical, so the walk always runs to the end, where §12.7's needed a trailing byte to force it), and a claim measured against another section's fixtures is not measured.

**The byte term.** `committed_field_shape_verdict_at_the_field_byte_bound` carries 32,768 bytes — §5.4's per-field bound, which is also `certified_chunks`' cap on a tier-3 `total_length`, so it is the largest committed preimage any carriage this family accepts can reach — as a single item on §8.4's chunked route at §8.3's `max_tier3_chunk_count` of three, and convicts it at slot 0 on §7.4. It measures 1,736,243 mem / 839,259,595 cpu against a fixture-only control of 1,020,085 / 521,630,867, so the rule's own share at the byte bound is about **716,158 memory units, 5.4% of the §3.3 memory basis**, and that figure already contains the three-chunk materialisation and the one `blake2b_256` over the whole preimage. The byte axis is not where this family runs out of budget.

**The item term, and why it has controls.** `committed_field_shape_verdict_at_{two_hundred_fifty,five_hundred}_items` read the same shape at 250 and 500 minimum-width items — §5.1's narrowest item is the empty one, `40` — committed at slot 0, where `header_len + 40·N` is nowhere near the preimage's own length and the verdict is `wrong_stride`. Their nets against the matching controls are 3,281,418 and 6,291,638 mem (839,870,169 and 1,601,488,723 cpu), which prices the walk-plus-verdict at **12,040.88 mem and 3,046,474.22 cpu per item** with an intercept of 271,198 mem / 78,251,615 cpu. **This family's own single-transaction ceiling is therefore about 1,073 items** — `(13,200,000 − 271,198) / 12,040.88` — and the memory axis binds, cpu at that cardinality being around 3.35G against the 8G basis. That figure is this lane's own arithmetic over this lane's own rows, and it was deliberately left unreconciled with the figure §12.7 published for its fixtures. **Both figures are readings (#580, 2026-08-15; re-read under #606, 2026-08-16), and the reconciliation is a measured two-item gap rather than two fits.** Bisected on the net memory axis with the pinned fork and pinned by four selectors in the measured module (`committed_field_shape_verdict_at_the_measured_item_ceiling` and `..._at_the_first_item_over_the_basis`, each with its fixture-only control), which are **not rows here** because their raw readings are about 24.1M mem and a within-basis ledger admits only rows whose raw reading fits: **this family's measured ceiling is 1,074 items** (net 13,193,414 mem / 3,347,103,163 cpu; row 24,106,075 / 6,702,341,195 against control 10,912,661 / 3,355,238,032) and **1,075** is the first over (net 13,205,438 mem / 3,350,143,255 cpu; row 24,127,481 / 6,708,088,467 against control 10,922,043 / 3,357,945,212). §12.7's twin measures **1,076**. The two-item gap is this family's higher intercept — the §7.4 stride arithmetic it asks after the same walk — and the fit is again one item low, 1,073 against the measured 1,074. #580 read this crossing one item higher, at 1,075/1,076, against the pre-#606 tree; the dated paragraph at the end of this note records the move and its cause. Memory binds at the crossing; cpu is 3.35G against the 8G basis.

The controls are not decoration. A row is a whole-test reading, and this lane's fixture is `encode_field_preimage` over a list whose length is the quantity being priced — a fold of `concat` whose own cost grows with it. Differencing the two rows alone gives 21,339 mem per item, nearly half of which is the producer. The controls remove it.

**The over-basis reading, and why it is not a row here.** The worst shape this family admits is §5.4's byte bound spent on minimum-width items: a three-byte array header and 32,765 one-byte items is exactly 32,768 bytes carrying 32,765 items, which the fit above puts at roughly **394,780,000 mem / 99,890,000,000 cpu** — 29.9x the §3.3 memory basis and 12.5x its cpu basis. It is not a row because a within-basis ledger records only `within` rows (see `exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs`), and the q1x-style `basisFit:"exceeds"` vocabulary requires an `errata` cross-reference into a normative erratum §12.8 does not carry. It is an **extrapolation, not a reading** — that is stated rather than glossed, and it remains the one number in this ledger that is not measured. #580 re-took it over the *measured* boundary pair rather than the 250/500 pair, which puts it at about **394,200,000 mem**, 29.9x the basis unchanged; re-derived over the #606 boundary pair it is 394,245,998 mem, the same figure at that precision. What #580 measured is the **ceiling** it extrapolates past, not the 32,765-item shape itself.

**The carriage ceiling, which no row here can move.** §12.8's §5.4 byte-bound shape is convictable by this family's *rule* at any length, and the §8 ladder cannot deliver a preimage above §5.4's bound to a step at all: `certified_chunks` refuses `total_length > max_transaction_aggregate_field_bytes` (`lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak`), the §8.6 certificate mint refuses the same bound before a certificate can exist (`verify_field_preimage_certificate_v1` in `lib/midgard/native-tx-carriage-v1.ak`), and tiers 1–2 are bounded by L1's `maxTxSize` far below it. So the byte-bound verdict is exercised here only by rule-level fixtures above the bound — the 32,768-byte row itself convicts on §7.4, not §5.4, since code 2 requires `total_length > 32,768` — and on the §8 ladder it is a rule with no carriage. That is a **carriage** fact rather than a cost fact — closing it is an §8 amendment, which this ticket does not take — and it is recorded in §12.8's own residue paragraph, on #601, and here so that a reader of these rows does not mistake the byte term for a claim that every §5.4 violation is provable on L1 today.

**What these rows do NOT claim.** (1) That the shapes measured are valid L2 transactions. They are the worst shapes *this family* admits, which is what bounds its cost: the step authenticates bytes against the operator's own committed hash and reads no item's content. (2) A machine-checked decomposition. The within-basis shape judges absolute rows and publishes no `derived` subtraction, so every net above is arithmetic a reader does over rows this file pins, not a number the gate checks. (3) That the step-01 *validator's* thread and inclusion machinery is priced. The rows measure `committed_field_shape_v1`, which is the family's own claim; the computation-thread and MPF membership costs it shares with every other native family are measured with those families.

Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-committed-field-shape-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. `--update` rewrites the raw mem/cpu rows; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, and it is not a bypass — a row or selector that did not run, or a fresh reading that contradicts a `within` judgement, fails in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten. Provisional on the same footing as every other ledger in this directory: formal closure is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint.

**#606 re-take, 2026-08-16 — the E2 certificate repair, and the ceiling falls to 1,074.** This lane moved under the #606 batch exactly as §12.7's twin did, by the same constants, and is recorded here on the same terms. Both halves are **bisected** against pristine `git archive` builds of the intervening commits; the blueprint identity is unmoved throughout (md5 `5e38d7c6ccb7987d0aca710307dcaea7`, 398 validators).

(1) **A constant +9,200 mem / +1,472,000 cpu on the rule's own share, at every cardinality**, charged by the E2 repair commit `d528e00b` — constant certificate asset name, mint-welded `field_hash`, the door's new equality against the commitment derived from the anchored structures, and the deletion of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor`. Measured to be constant, not fitted to be: both cardinality rows moved by exactly that while their fixture-only controls did not move by a unit, the marginal across the boundary pair is 12,024 mem / 3,040,092 cpu per item as before, and only the intercept rose (261,998 → 271,198 mem, 76,779,615 → 78,251,615 cpu). That the **same** two integers land on both this family and §12.7's — two different fixtures, two different verdicts, one shared door — is what makes the shift the door's rather than either walk's. The pexcludes rider `139a8ca3` costs this family nothing: its readings are identical to the batch base `854fea09` to the unit. No decomposition of the constant across the repair's four changes is published, because these rows carry `Inline` tier-1 carriage at a body field and do not execute the certificate branch at all.

**The consequence, stated as the downward correction it is.** #580's margin at 1,075 items was 3,762 memory units, which a constant +9,200 consumes: 1,075 now nets 13,205,438 mem and is **over** the §3.3 basis. The crossing was re-bisected, the four boundary selectors re-pinned at 1,074 / 1,075 in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/committed-field-shape/rule.test.ak`, and this family's published ceiling moves **down one item, 1,075 → 1,074**. The two-item gap against §12.7 survives the move (1,074 against 1,076), which is what a constant common to both families predicts and is the check that the two re-readings are one measurement rather than two coincidences.

(2) **+200 mem / +32,000 cpu on the byte-bound row alone**, charged by `3eb41df7` (the §8.6 certificate field-index bound routed through `field_count`), measured at `2a64d6f9` → `3eb41df7` with the fixture-only control unmoved, and paid once per door opening that decodes a certificate datum. It landed after the batch's first ledger re-take (`7158377e`) and left this ledger red until this re-take. The byte-bound row's whole movement from the pre-batch 1,741,698 / 806,467,398 is therefore **−5,455 mem / +32,792,197 cpu** — the same pair §12.7's twin records — and its net share is now about 716,158 memory units, 5.4% of the basis where this note previously published 5.5%.

No `basisFit` moved: every row here was and remains `within`. The **carriage ceiling** paragraph above is untouched by all of this and one sentence of it is now differently framed: §8.3 erratum E2 limit 3 no longer refuses tier-3 carriage anywhere, since #606 resolved it, so the reason a preimage above §5.4's bound cannot reach a step is `certified_chunks`' and the §8.6 mint's own `max_transaction_aggregate_field_bytes` refusals alone — which is what that paragraph already rests on.

The movement from the previously pinned rows is NOT compiler-caused. Every row fell by exactly 3 CEK machine steps: the CEK step cost is a constant `mem: 100, cpu: 16000` (`default_machine_cost()` in the fork's `crates/uplc/src/machine/cost_model.rs`), so -300/-48,000 is 3 steps and nothing else. The cause is source, not codegen: `c2237b30` (feat(fault-proofs): complete missing-signature lifecycle) rewrote `onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/field-opening-v1.ak`, adding `resume_opened_field_walk` over the machine-walk resume entry point, which shortens the field-opening path by that fixed step count. The same per-opening quantum (-300 mem / -48,000 cpu) appears in the canonical-decodability ledger, where a control re-measurement under that ledger's own former rev `2a78108` reproduced the identical shift, establishing the movement as source drift rather than a compiler difference. All three published nets are unchanged to the unit: the shift is common to each row and its `fixture_only` control, so real-minus-control cancels it exactly (716,158 / 317,628,728 at the field-byte bound; 3,281,418 / 839,870,169 at 250 items; 6,291,638 / 1,601,488,723 at 500 items). basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3 — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. Provenance, exactly as §3.3 states it: the captured in-repo artifact is the mainnet parameter snapshot in docs/midgard/decisions/0001-cardano-l1-transaction-capability-floor.md, Conway epoch 645, observed 2026-07-24.

modules.neutralisationNote: Both selectors are mutation-verified rather than assumed. (1) `committed_field_shape_ledger_fixture_sits_at_the_field_byte_bound` is the shape guard, and it is why a re-take cannot quietly re-pin a cheaper row: it asserts the bound fixture is exactly `max_transaction_aggregate_field_bytes` bytes, above §8.3's `K`, at `expected_chunk_count == max_tier3_chunk_count`, a §5.1 envelope (so the walk really runs to the end), convicted on §7.4 at slot 0, and a single item; and that both cardinality fixtures fit tier 1, are grammatical, convict on §7.4, and differ in item count alone. Shrink any of them and this selector goes red before the row is re-pinned. (2) `committed_field_shape_verdict_refuses_substituted_certified_chunks` is the discrimination guard: neutralising `expect field_commitment(preimage) == expected_hash` in `authenticated_committed_preimage` (`lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak`) turns it red, and the check report names that exact line as the failure it traps. The vector is honest about isolating that one guard — the certificate is one a real certification produced, its digest vector is over the real chunks, every named chunk is the right length and the count is the derived one — so every §8.4/§8.6 check `certified_chunks` runs still passes and only §4's hash separates the substituted bytes from the committed ones. It is also what makes the bound row's tier-3 carriage falsifiable. The family's other guards — the §2.5 body/witness pairing, the fabricated verdict and field index, the forged transactions root, the foreign next-step hash, the honest-block negative and the §12.7 disjointness refusal — are covered by the small-shape selectors in the two validator modules, because a 32,768-byte fixture isolates none of them better than a six-byte one does.
